body: Soil organic carbon (SOC) is an indicator of agricultural soil condition and carbon storage, but numerical outputs from large language models (LLMs) require validation before use in monitoring or management. We evaluated seven general-purpose LLM configurations on three direct-response tasks: estimating 0--10 cm SOC concentrations for 308 Australian paddocks under two information conditions, calculating SOC stock in 120 matched scenarios, and comparing 300 paddock pairs. References were measured SOC records or deterministic calculations; response validity, repeated-call dispersion and estimated API cost were assessed separately. Additional measured soil attributes reduced concentration mean absolute error by 13--62% across configurations, although high-SOC underprediction and paddock-specific errors persisted. Six configurations were highly accurate in stock calculations using equation-native units without coarse fragments, but accuracy declined with physically equivalent alternative units. Pairwise accuracy was 90.5--94.6% overall and 59.1--70.9% for 52 closely separated pairs; some configurations were sensitive to presentation order. Nearly all outputs were parseable, without necessarily being correct. The benchmark identifies three distinct requirements for AI-mediated SOC assessment: agreement with measured concentrations, unit-consistent stock calculations and reliable discrimination between sites. These findings support task-specific validation and auditable calculations, rather than unverified use of LLM outputs as ecological evidence.
summaryZh: 本文针对大语言模型在土壤有机碳（SOC）评估中的应用进行了系统性基准测试。研究评估了七种 LLM 配置在浓度估算、储量计算及场地对比任务中的表现。结果显示，虽然模型在特定计算任务中表现出高准确性，但对单位敏感且存在特定偏差。该研究强调了在生态科学领域应用 LLM 时，必须进行任务特定的验证与可审计计算，不能直接将模型输出视为可靠的科学证据，为科学领域 AI 应用的规范化提供了重要参考。
